description: Documents the specific error scenario of API-057 (Create Payment) where transactionReference duplicates an existing payment. Same endpoint as API-057, isolated here to preserve the original docs/API_Contracts_and_Test_Results.xlsx functionality numbering. This is a confirmed DB GAP.

body.transactionReference: 'TXN0001' - duplicate of an existing payment's transactionReference in this scenario

validation: transactionReference should be unique per the intended API contract

success.status_definition: N/A - this functionality ID documents only the failure path; see API-057 for the success contract

errors.condition: transactionReference already exists on another payment

constraints: transaction_reference VARCHAR(100) - nullable, no UNIQUE constraint or index in the current schema

notes: database/schema/026_payment.sql defines transaction_reference as a plain nullable VARCHAR(100) with no UNIQUE constraint or index anywhere in the schema (verified through database/schema/versions/v25.sql). database/api_contracts_test/015_payment.sql's API-T123 scenario confirms a second payment with the same transaction_reference ('TXN0001') is currently accepted by PostgreSQL, even though the intended API behavior is 409 Conflict. A UNIQUE constraint/index on (organization_id, branch_id, transaction_reference) - or a narrower scope if transaction references are meant to be globally unique across a payment gateway - would need to be added to actually enforce this at the DB layer; until then, duplicate detection must happen at the API layer only. This same missing constraint is also the root cause of the 'UPDATE 2' anomaly noted in API-059 and API-068.
